events.continuity_hook: This begins Erin's first post-Thanksgiving work trip after the Milwaukee family visit is complete.
events.interaction_goal: Build a ranked plan for arrival day, flight routing, hotel area, rental-car timing, recovery amenities, parking, and the schedule questions to confirm before booking.
events.scenario_brief: After Thanksgiving, Erin is assigned a mid-December Pacific Northwest rollout for a small hospital group with planned sessions in Beaverton, Vancouver, and Lake Oswego, plus a possible Monday calibration. She will have a demo analyzer case and workbook cartons, so a rental car with easy hotel parking matters more than restaurant access. A Sunday afternoon Denver-to-Portland nonstop gives the cleanest setup, while a Monday morning one-stop is cheaper but risky if calibration is added. Hotel candidates include a Beaverton suite property with strong reviews, parking, pool, and fitness access but no hot tub, an airport hotel with the full recovery-amenity set but longer drives, and a downtown Portland hotel with better dining but paid parking and more traffic. The clinic order, Monday requirement, shipped-kit status, and Thursday return window remain unresolved.

events.continuity_hook: This narrows the Pacific Northwest plan once the Monday calibration and clinic sequence become firm.
events.interaction_goal: Choose the flights, settle the hotel, plan rental pickup and drop-off, note the missing hot tub, and prepare booking steps for seats, room request, and expense notes.
events.scenario_brief: The coordinator confirms Monday calibration near Beaverton at 3:30 p.m., Tuesday training in Beaverton, Wednesday clinic work in Vancouver, and Thursday hands-on work in Lake Oswego ending around 2:00 p.m. The Sunday afternoon nonstop now beats the cheaper Monday one-stop, and a compact SUV is sensible for the demo case and workbook cartons. The Beaverton suite hotel can hold a quiet king room with parking, a fridge, pool, and fitness access, though it still lacks a hot tub; the airport hotel has the hot tub but adds more driving on every clinic day. The open choice is whether to attempt a Thursday evening return after pack-up or add one more hotel night for a Friday morning nonstop.

events.continuity_hook: This closes the Pacific Northwest planning after Erin chose the calmer Friday return and the Beaverton suite hotel.
events.interaction_goal: Run the final logistics pass for airport timing, rental pickup, wet-weather packing, demo-case handling, daily drive buffers, hotel arrival, return seat selection, and Friday checkout.
events.scenario_brief: Four days before departing for Portland, Erin has booked the Sunday afternoon nonstop, the Beaverton suite hotel through Friday checkout, a compact SUV, and the Friday morning return. The airline has moved the outbound 45 minutes later, but the arrival still leaves room for hotel check-in and Monday calibration prep. A wet forecast could slow drives to Vancouver and Lake Oswego, the main demo analyzer has arrived at the Beaverton clinic, and one consumables carton will travel in her checked bag. The hotel confirms the quiet-room request, pool, and fitness room, but no hot tub; the return seat map changed after an aircraft swap and her window seat is no longer assigned.

events.continuity_hook: This shifts Erin from December clinic travel into a January conference with a possible leisure extension.
events.interaction_goal: Create a ranked plan for flight dates, expo arrival timing, work-only versus weekend-stay returns, hotel area, spouse add-on feasibility, and local transportation.
events.scenario_brief: After the Portland rollout and the holiday lull, Erin starts planning a late-January veterinary diagnostics expo in San Diego. Booth duty is expected Tuesday through Thursday near the convention center, with a possible Monday setup and an optional Friday continuing-education session; her spouse may join for a Friday-to-Sunday coastal add-on if PTO works. A Monday afternoon Denver-to-San Diego nonstop would fit if setup is confirmed, while arriving Tuesday morning is likely too tight and a Sunday arrival may be more hotel than she needs. Lodging choices include the official downtown block with the shortest walk and high rate, a bayfront hotel with pool, hot tub, fitness access, and some balcony rooms but rideshare or trolley time, and a Mission Valley option with a lower rate and easy parking. The final agenda, spouse timing, hotel-block deadline, and need for a rental car remain open.

events.continuity_hook: This follows the first San Diego expo pass once the agenda and spouse PTO become clearer.
events.interaction_goal: Finalize the outbound and return flights, spouse flight timing, hotel booking, room request, seat selections, and whether rideshares are enough for the weekend add-on.
events.scenario_brief: The expo agenda is finalized: Monday setup runs 4:00 to 6:00 p.m., booth hours are Tuesday through Thursday, and the Friday education session ends at noon. Erin's spouse can fly in Friday afternoon and stay until Sunday, so the plan shifts from a simple work return to a mixed work-and-weekend stay. The early-afternoon Monday nonstop from Denver gives enough margin without making her leave before dawn, and the Sunday afternoon return keeps Monday clear. The bayfront hotel can offer a king room for the full stay with pool, hot tub, fitness access, and requestable balcony rooms; the downtown block is more convenient for booth mornings but pricier and less relaxing for the weekend. The rental-car question is still unresolved because parking fees could outweigh the convenience for one coastal outing.

events.continuity_hook: This is a post-booking San Diego adjustment after the conference schedule becomes less convenient for the bayfront stay.
events.interaction_goal: Compare the single-hotel and split-stay plans, account for commute time and amenity trade-offs, and decide what to modify before cancellation windows tighten.
events.scenario_brief: Erin has booked the Monday outbound, Sunday return, and bayfront hotel, with her spouse on a separate Friday afternoon outbound. The conference adds a mandatory 7:00 a.m. Wednesday breakfast and a Thursday evening teardown window, making the bayfront commute less attractive on the heaviest work days. At the same time, the bayfront hotel says balcony rooms are request-only and the hot tub will be closed until Friday afternoon; a downtown block room has reopened for Monday through Thursday but would require a split stay before the weekend. The remaining decision is whether to keep the single hotel for simplicity, split work nights downtown and weekend nights on the bay, or accept extra rideshares and keep the existing booking.
